requirement: Parse event timestamps arriving with mixed UTC offsets into one UTC timeline, setting aside rows whose timestamp cannot be parsed instead of failing the whole batch.
skeleton: normalize_events converting ts with to_datetime utc True and errors coerce, splitting NaT rows into a reindexed quarantine frame, and returning parsed rows sorted by instant.
caption: Cleaning event timestamps with pandas when sources mix UTC offsets and send garbage. normalize_events(events) parses the ts column with pd.to_datetime using utc True, errors coerce and format ISO8601, so every offset becomes one UTC timezone-aware instant and unparseable, empty or missing values become NaT. Rows with NaT form the quarantine frame, returned with their original string values and a fresh zero-based index. The remaining rows get the parsed ts assigned, are sorted by ts with a stable sort, and have their index renumbered. It returns the clean and bad frames as a tuple and never modifies the input. The fixture asserts that the clean timestamps are in UTC at 08:00, 09:30 and 12:00, that clean ids are 1, 2, 3 with index 0 to 2, that ids 90, 91 and 92 are quarantined with index 0 to 2 keeping the raw not a date text, and that the input frame is unchanged.

constraints: Mixed offsets are converted to one UTC timezone
Unparseable values become NaT instead of raising
NaT rows are returned separately with raw text and a fresh index
Clean rows are sorted by instant with a fresh index
The input frame is not modified

rationale.teaches: Combine utc True with errors coerce so mixed offsets parse into comparable instants and bad values are quarantined rather than crashing ingestion.
rationale.why: Without utc mixed offsets cannot share one dtype, errors raise kills the batch on one bad row, and sorting raw strings orders by local wall time.

ops.docstring: Normalize event timestamps to UTC and quarantine unparseable ones.

ops.source:
def normalize_events(events: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return (events sorted by UTC timestamp, rows whose timestamp is invalid)."""
    ts = pd.to_datetime(events["ts"], utc=True, errors="coerce", format="ISO8601")
    bad = ts.isna()
    clean = events.loc[~bad].assign(ts=ts[~bad])
    clean = clean.sort_values("ts", kind="stable", ignore_index=True)
    return clean, events.loc[bad].reset_index(drop=True)

candidates.why_wrong: Mixed UTC offsets fail to parse into a single timezone-aware column.
One unparseable timestamp aborts the whole batch with an exception.
Clean events stay in arrival order instead of chronological order.
Quarantined rows keep their original index labels instead of zero-based ones.
Clean rows keep raw strings, so sorting follows local wall-clock text.
